Diodotus II.answer: Diodotus II Theos (Greek: Διόδοτος Θεός, Diódotos Theós, "Diodotus the God"; r. Diodotus II probably ruled alongside his father as co-regent, before s
Diodotus II.fact: Diodotus II Theos (Greek: Διόδοτος Θεός, Diódotos Theós, "Diodotus the God"; r. Diodotus II probably ruled alongside his father as co-regent, before succeeding him as sole king around 235 BC.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: 235 – 225 BC) was the son and successor of Diodotus I Soter, who rebelled against the _____, establishing the Graeco-Bactrian Kingdom
Diodotus II.fact: 235 – 225 BC) was the son and successor of Diodotus I Soter, who rebelled against the Seleucid Empire, establishing the Graeco-Bactrian Kingdom.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: He prevented _____ efforts to reincorporate Bactria back into the empire, by allying with the Parthians against them
Diodotus II.fact: 235 – 225 BC) was the son and successor of Diodotus I Soter, who rebelled against the Seleucid Empire, establishing the Graeco-Bactrian Kingdom. He prevented Seleucid efforts to reincorporate Bactria back into the empire, by allying with the Parthians against them.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: He was murdered around 225 BC by _____ I, who succeeded him as king
Diodotus II.fact: He was murdered around 225 BC by Euthydemus I, who succeeded him as king.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Diodotus's career was recounted by _____ of Artemita in the Parthian History, but this text is lost, and surviving literary sources only mention him in passing
Diodotus II.fact: Diodotus's career was recounted by Apollodorus of Artemita in the Parthian History, but this text is lost, and surviving literary sources only mention him in passing.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Arsaces had gone on to seize the region of _____ from the Seleucids and carved out his own kingdom in what is now northeastern Iran
Diodotus II.fact: The location of the region under Diodotus II's control is unknown; Holt tentatively suggests that he controlled the western region which was exposed to raids from Parthia and had his base at Bactra. Arsaces had gone on to seize the region of Parthia from the Seleucids and carved out his own kingdom in what is now northeastern Iran.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Diodotus I remained opposed to the Parni and thus aligned with the _____
Diodotus II.fact: This arrangement would follow the model laid down by the Seleucids, who had made a practice of appointing the crown prince as co-regent and entrusting them with government of the eastern portion of the empire (including Bactria). Arsaces had gone on to seize the region of Parthia from the Seleucids and carved out his own kingdom in what is now northeastern Iran.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: It is unclear whether Diodotus was actively involved in the battle or simply agreed to remain neutral, thereby leaving _____ free to bring all his forces to bear on the invading Seleucid army
Diodotus II.fact: Arsaces had gone on to seize the region of Parthia from the Seleucids and carved out his own kingdom in what is now northeastern Iran. On his accession, Diodotus II reversed his father's policy: Soon after, relieved by the death of Diodotus [I], Arsaces made peace and concluded an alliance with his son, also by the name of Diodotus; some time later he fought against Seleucus [II] who came to punish the rebels, but he prevailed: the Parthians celebrated this day as the one that marked the begi...

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Sometime after this, around 225 BC, Diodotus was killed by _____ I, who usurped the throne and founded the Euthydemid dynasty
Diodotus II.fact: Sometime after this, around 225 BC, Diodotus was killed by Euthydemus I, who usurped the throne and set up the Euthydemid dynasty. W. W. Tarn proposed that Diodotus I had married a Seleucid princess as a second wife and had a daughter who was married to Euthydemus, making him Diodotus II's brother-in-law.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Archaeological evidence reveals that the city of Ai-_____ was besieged around 225 BC, an event which Holt connects with Euthydemus's seizure of power
Diodotus II.fact: Archaeological evidence reveals that the city of Ai-Khanoum was besieged around 225 BC, an event which Holt connects with Euthydemus's seizure of power.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: It seems therefore that there was a period of civil war, culminating in _____'s victory—a reconstruction that seems to be confirmed by numismatic evidence
Diodotus II.fact: W. W. Tarn proposed that Diodotus I had married a Seleucid princess as a second wife and had a daughter who was married to Euthydemus, making him Diodotus II's brother-in-law. Archaeological evidence reveals that the city of Ai-Khanoum was besieged around 225 BC, an event which Holt connects with Euthydemus's seizure of power.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Most scholars have treated the alliance with _____ as a response to the threat from Seleucus II
Diodotus II.fact: Most scholars have treated the alliance with Arsaces as a response to the threat from Seleucus II. Frank Holt proposes the opposite: that the alliance with Arsaces was a response to the outbreak of civil war with Euthydemus.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Frank Holt proposes the opposite: that the alliance with _____ was a response to the outbreak of civil war with Euthydemus
Diodotus II.fact: Most scholars have treated the alliance with Arsaces as a response to the threat from Seleucus II. Frank Holt proposes the opposite: that the alliance with Arsaces was a response to the outbreak of civil war with Euthydemus.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Tarn suggested that _____ I's usurpation was a reaction to the alliance
Diodotus II.fact: Archaeological evidence reveals that the city of Ai-Khanoum was besieged around 225 BC, an event which Holt connects with Euthydemus's seizure of power. It seems therefore that there was a period of civil war, culminating in Euthydemus's victory—a reconstruction that seems to be confirmed by numismatic evidence.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: The precious metal coinage consisted of gold staters and silver tetradrachms, drachms, and hemidrachms on the _____ weight standard
Diodotus II.fact: The precious metal coinage consisted of gold staters and silver tetradrachms, drachms, and hemidrachms on the Attic weight standard.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: The reverse of these coins depicted _____ preparing to throw his thunderbolt
Diodotus II.fact: The reverse of these coins depicted Zeus preparing to throw his thunderbolt.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Series A and C probably minted at Ai-_____ or at Bactra, while Series E was minted at a second mint, which Frank Holt tentatively identifies with Bactra
Diodotus II.fact: Series A and C probably minted at Ai-Khanoum or at Bactra, while Series E was minted at a second mint, which Frank Holt tentatively identifies with Bactra. This mint produced coinage in a smaller quantity and at a lower quality than that of the Ai-Khanoum/Bactra mint.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: This mint produced coinage in a smaller quantity and at a lower quality than that of the Ai-_____/Bactra mint
Diodotus II.fact: Series A and C probably minted at Ai-Khanoum or at Bactra, while Series E was minted at a second mint, which Frank Holt tentatively identifies with Bactra. This mint produced coinage in a smaller quantity and at a lower quality than that of the Ai-Khanoum/Bactra mint.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: This shift in legends seems to reflect the final renunciation of _____ authority and a full proclamation of Bactrian independence
Diodotus II.fact: This shift in legends seems to reflect the final renunciation of Seleucid authority and a full proclamation of Bactrian independence.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Initially, this coinage bore the same obverse design as that of Diodotus I: head of _____ wearing a petasus hat ('Series H')
Diodotus II.fact: Initially, this coinage bore the same obverse design as that of Diodotus I: head of Hermes wearing a petasus hat ('Series H').

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: Only the first two of these denominations seem to be attested under _____ value of these denominations is uncertain; a single may have been worth 1/48 of a silver drachm
Diodotus II.fact: Only the first two of these denominations seem to be attested under Diodotus I. The value of these denominations is uncertain; a single may have been worth 1/48 of a silver drachm.

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: After this initial issue, Diodotus introduced a new set of designs ('_____ I')
Diodotus II.fact: After this initial issue, Diodotus introduced a new set of designs ('Series I').

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: On the double and single denominations, these depict the head of Zeus on the obverse (except on one issue depicting a king—probably by accident), and the goddess _____ on the reverse
Diodotus II.fact: On the double and single denominations, these depict the head of Zeus on the obverse (except on one issue depicting a king—probably by accident), and the goddess Artemis on the reverse. On the quarters, they have an eagle on the obverse and a quiver on the reverse (symbols of Zeus and Artemis respectively).

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: On the quarters, they have an eagle on the obverse and a quiver on the reverse (symbols of Zeus and _____ respectively)
Diodotus II.fact: On the double and single denominations, these depict the head of Zeus on the obverse (except on one issue depicting a king—probably by accident), and the goddess Artemis on the reverse. On the quarters, they have an eagle on the obverse and a quiver on the reverse (symbols of Zeus and Artemis respectively).

Diodotus II.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus II.question: These bronze coins were found in very large numbers in the excavations of Ai-_____ and in smaller quantities at Gyaur Gala (Merv, Turkmenistan) and Takht-i Sangin
Diodotus II.fact: These bronze coins were found in very large numbers in the excavations of Ai-Khanoum and in smaller quantities at Gyaur Gala (Merv, Turkmenistan) and Takht-i Sangin.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: What do you know about Diodotus Tryphon (Greek: Διόδοτος Τρύφων, Diódotos Trýphōn), nicknamed "The Magn?
Diodotus Tryphon.answer: a Greek king of the Seleucid Empire.
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Diodotus Tryphon (Greek: Διόδοτος Τρύφων, Diódotos Trýphōn), nicknamed "The Magnificent" (Greek: Ό Μεγαλοπρεπής) was a Greek king of the Seleucid Empire.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Initially an official under _____ I Balas, he led a revolt against Alexander's successor Demetrius II Nicator in 144 BC
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Initially an official under King Alexander I Balas, he led a revolt against Alexander's successor Demetrius II Nicator in 144 BC.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: He rapidly gained control of most of Syria and the _____
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: He rapidly gained control of most of Syria and the Levant.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: At first, he acted as regent and tutor for _____'s infant son Antiochus VI Dionysus, but after the death of his charge in 142/141 BC, Diodotus declared himself king
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Initially an official under King Alexander I Balas, he led a revolt against Alexander's successor Demetrius II Nicator in 144 BC. At first, he acted as regent and tutor for Alexander's infant son Antiochus VI Dionysus, but after the death of his charge in 142/141 BC, Diodotus declared himself king.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: He took the royal name _____ (Greek: Τρύφων Αὐτοκράτωρ) and distanced himself from the Seleucid dynasty
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: He took the royal name Tryphon Autocrator (Greek: Τρύφων Αὐτοκράτωρ) and distanced himself from the Seleucid dynasty.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: For a period between 139 and 138, he was the sole ruler of the _____ empire
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: He took the royal name Tryphon Autocrator (Greek: Τρύφων Αὐτοκράτωρ) and distanced himself from the Seleucid dynasty. For a period between 139 and 138, he was the sole ruler of the Seleucid empire.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: However, in 138 BC _____ II's brother Antiochus VII Sidetes invaded Syria and brought his rule to an end
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: However, in 138 BC Demetrius II's brother Antiochus VII Sidetes invaded Syria and brought his rule to an end.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: He served as a general for _____, during the civil war which the latter fought with Demetrius II Nicator
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: He served as a general for Alexander Balas, during the civil war which the latter fought with Demetrius II Nicator.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: In 145 BC, when _____'s father-in-law Ptolemy VI of Egypt switched his support to Demetrius II and invaded Syria, Diodotus and a man called Hierax were in command of the city of Antioch
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: He served as a general for Alexander Balas, during the civil war which the latter fought with Demetrius II Nicator. In 145 BC, when Alexander's father-in-law Ptolemy VI of Egypt switched his support to Demetrius II and invaded Syria, Diodotus and a man called Hierax were in command of the city of Antioch.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: They surrendered _____ to Ptolemy and declared him king of the Seleucid Empire
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: In 145 BC, when Alexander's father-in-law Ptolemy VI of Egypt switched his support to Demetrius II and invaded Syria, Diodotus and a man called Hierax were in command of the city of Antioch. They surrendered Antioch to Ptolemy and declared him king of the Seleucid Empire.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Ptolemy, unwilling to rule both the _____ and Seleucid realms directly, declined the title in favour of Demetrius II
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Ptolemy, unwilling to rule both the Egyptian and Seleucid realms directly, declined the title in favour of Demetrius II.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Revolt against Demetrius II _____ II secured himself on the throne, he began to eliminate former associates of Alexander Balas
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Revolt against Demetrius II As Demetrius II secured himself on the throne, he began to eliminate former associates of Alexander Balas.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: He probably considered himself to be in danger, and he fled to an Arab ruler called _____ or Imalkue, who had been entrusted with the care of Alexander Balas's young son
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: He probably considered himself to be in danger, and he fled to an Arab ruler called Zabdiel or Imalkue, who had been entrusted with the care of Alexander Balas's young son.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Diodotus, with Arab support, declared _____'s son the new king, as Antiochus VI Dionysus
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Revolt against Demetrius II As Demetrius II secured himself on the throne, he began to eliminate former associates of Alexander Balas. Diodotus (Trypho) is introduced in the First Book of Maccabees as "a certain Trypho [who] had formerly been one of Alexander’s supporters", who sees and seizes an opportunity when "he saw that all the troops were grumbling against Demetrius [II]".

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Diodotus and _____ were initially ignored by Demetrius who had to consolidate his power and was also faced with financial troubles
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Diodotus, with Arab support, declared Alexander's son the new king, as Antiochus VI Dionysus. Diodotus and Antiochus were initially ignored by Demetrius who had to consolidate his power and was also faced with financial troubles.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Utilising the discontent against the ruling regime Diodotus gathered a large army at his headquarters in _____ ad Belum
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Utilising the discontent against the ruling regime Diodotus gathered a large army at his headquarters in Chalcis ad Belum. Diodotus, in the name of the boy-king Antiochus VI, controlled most of Inland Syria, including Antioch, Apamea, Larisa and Chalcis.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Eventually, _____ marched against them but he was defeated in battle, after which Diodotus gained control of Apamea and Antioch
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Diodotus and Antiochus were initially ignored by Demetrius who had to consolidate his power and was also faced with financial troubles. Eventually, Demetrius marched against them but he was defeated in battle, after which Diodotus gained control of Apamea and Antioch.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Numismatic evidence indicates that Apamea was taken in early 144 and _____ in late 144 or early 143
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Diodotus and Antiochus were initially ignored by Demetrius who had to consolidate his power and was also faced with financial troubles. Eventually, Demetrius marched against them but he was defeated in battle, after which Diodotus gained control of Apamea and Antioch.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Diodotus, in the name of the boy-king _____ VI, controlled most of Inland Syria, including Antioch, Apamea, Larisa and Chalcis
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Diodotus, in the name of the boy-king Antiochus VI, controlled most of Inland Syria, including Antioch, Apamea, Larisa and Chalcis.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Demetrius on the other hand based himself in _____ and retained control of many of the Syrian and Phoenician coastal cities and Cilicia
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Demetrius on the other hand based himself in Seleucia Pieria and retained control of many of the Syrian and Phoenician coastal cities and Cilicia.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Mesopotamia continued to recognise _____ as well and an invasion of the region by Diodotus in mid-144 seems to have been a failure
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Demetrius on the other hand based himself in Seleucia Pieria and retained control of many of the Syrian and Phoenician coastal cities and Cilicia. Mesopotamia continued to recognise Demetrius as well and an invasion of the region by Diodotus in mid-144 seems to have been a failure.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Territories further east, such as Susa and _____ were conquered by the Parthians, who eventually took control of Mesopotamia as well in mid-141 BC
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Territories further east, such as Susa and Elymais were conquered by the Parthians, who eventually took control of Mesopotamia as well in mid-141 BC.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Josephus justifies this by claiming that _____ had persecuted the Jews and that the memory of Alexander Balas encouraged them to support his son Antiochus VI
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Intervention in Judaea At the same time Diodotus made diplomatic overtures to the Jews under Jonathan Apphus in order to have them join with him against Demetrius, giving him honours and appointing his brother Simon Thassi as general. Josephus justifies this by claiming that Demetrius had persecuted the Jews and that the memory of Alexander Balas encouraged them to support his son Antiochus VI.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: The Jewish sources claim that the boldness of the _____'s attacks on Demetrius' supporters led Diodotus to fear his power and begin to plot against him
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Jonathan accepted these overtures. The Jewish sources claim that the boldness of the Jonathan's attacks on Demetrius' supporters led Diodotus to fear his power and begin to plot against him.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: In 142 BC, Diodotus dispatched troops who lured _____ to Ptolemais with a small guard and captured him
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: The Jewish sources claim that the boldness of the Jonathan's attacks on Demetrius' supporters led Diodotus to fear his power and begin to plot against him. In 142 BC, Diodotus dispatched troops who lured Jonathan to Ptolemais with a small guard and captured him.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Although Simon Thassi paid the money that Diodotus had demanded as a ransom for his brother, Diodotus had him executed anyway and attempted to attack _____
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Although Simon Thassi paid the money that Diodotus had demanded as a ransom for his brother, Diodotus had him executed anyway and attempted to attack Jerusalem.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Heavy snowfall forced him to abandon the siege and return to _____
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Heavy snowfall forced him to abandon the siege and return to Syria.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Simon quickly became a close ally of _____, who granted extensive freedoms to him - later seen as the moment when the Hasmonean Jewish state achieved full independence
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Simon quickly became a close ally of Demetrius II, who granted extensive freedoms to him - later seen as the moment when the Hasmonean Jewish state achieved full independence.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Royal titles and representation As king, Diodotus used the name _____
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Royal titles and representation As king, Diodotus used the name Tryphon Autocrator.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: 'Tryphon' referred to the _____ royal virtue of tryphe (luxury)
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: 'Tryphon' referred to the Hellenistic royal virtue of tryphe (luxury).

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: The epithet _____ is unique; it is not attested for any other Greek ruler from this period
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: The epithet Autokrator is unique; it is not attested for any other Greek ruler from this period. Edwyn Bevan argued that this epithet was intended to recall the Macedonian kings Philip II and Alexander the Great, who had held the title of Strategos Autokrator as elected leaders of the Greek forces against Persia.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: There is no sign that Tryphon considered himself to be part of the _____ dynasty
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: There is no sign that Tryphon considered himself to be part of the Seleucid dynasty. On the contrary, he emphasised the break with his Seleucid predecessors through his unusual title, as well as the iconography of his coinage.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: On the contrary, he emphasised the break with his _____ predecessors through his unusual title, as well as the iconography of his coinage
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: There is no sign that Tryphon considered himself to be part of the Seleucid dynasty. On the contrary, he emphasised the break with his Seleucid predecessors through his unusual title, as well as the iconography of his coinage.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: His coins depicts him in a mature guise, with a rather fat face and long flowing hair - emphasising the luxuriousness implied by the name _____
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: His coins depicts him in a mature guise, with a rather fat face and long flowing hair - emphasising the luxuriousness implied by the name Trypon.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: The reverse side of his coins depict an elaborately decorated _____ helmet
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: The reverse side of his coins depict an elaborately decorated Boeotian helmet.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: In order to secure _____ recognition of his kingship, Tryphon sent a golden statue of the goddess Nike to Rome
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: In order to secure Roman recognition of his kingship, Tryphon sent a golden statue of the goddess Nike to Rome. The Roman Senate chose to accept this Nike as a gift from Antiochus VI and did not extend recognition to Tryphon.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: The Roman Senate chose to accept this Nike as a gift from _____ VI and did not extend recognition to Tryphon
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: The Roman Senate chose to accept this Nike as a gift from Antiochus VI and did not extend recognition to Tryphon. War against Demetrius II and Antiochus VII Once he was king, Tryphon expanded his control to at least Ptolemais-Akke and Dor.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: War against _____ II and Antiochus VII Once he was king, Tryphon expanded his control to at least Ptolemais-Akke and Dor
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: War against Demetrius II and Antiochus VII Once he was king, Tryphon expanded his control to at least Ptolemais-Akke and Dor. Demetrius, meanwhile, had journeyed east in 139/8 to fight the Parthians, who had seized control of Mesopotamia the previous year.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Almost immediately, however, _____' brother, Antiochus VII Sidetes took up the conflict against Tryphon
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: War against Demetrius II and Antiochus VII Once he was king, Tryphon expanded his control to at least Ptolemais-Akke and Dor. Demetrius, meanwhile, had journeyed east in 139/8 to fight the Parthians, who had seized control of Mesopotamia the previous year.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Demetrius, meanwhile, had journeyed east in 139/8 to fight the _____, who had seized control of Mesopotamia the previous year
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Demetrius, meanwhile, had journeyed east in 139/8 to fight the Parthians, who had seized control of Mesopotamia the previous year.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: He was defeated and captured by them July or _____ of 138 BC, leaving Tryphon as uncontested ruler of the remaining Seleucid territories
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: He was defeated and captured by them July or August of 138 BC, leaving Tryphon as uncontested ruler of the remaining Seleucid territories.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: He declared himself _____, left his home in Rhodes, and landed in Phoenicia in the face of staunch resistance
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: He declared himself King Antiochus Euergetes, left his home in Rhodes, and landed in Phoenicia in the face of staunch resistance.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: He married the wife of _____, Cleopatra Thea, further legitimizing his position
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Almost immediately, however, Demetrius' brother, Antiochus VII Sidetes took up the conflict against Tryphon. He married the wife of Demetrius, Cleopatra Thea, further legitimizing his position.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Numismatic evidence shows that many coastal cities remained loyal to Tryphon, but that Sidon and Tyre immediately attached themselves to _____' cause
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Almost immediately, however, Demetrius' brother, Antiochus VII Sidetes took up the conflict against Tryphon. He declared himself King Antiochus Euergetes, left his home in Rhodes, and landed in Phoenicia in the face of staunch resistance.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: Antiochus also successfully won over _____ by confirming and augmenting the grants made by his brother
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: Antiochus also successfully won over Simon Thassi by confirming and augmenting the grants made by his brother.

Diodotus Tryphon.subject: Ancient India
Diodotus Tryphon.question: From there he escaped by sea to _____ and made his way to his home-region of Apamea, where he was besieged again
Diodotus Tryphon.fact: From there he escaped by sea to Orthosia and made his way to his home-region of Apamea, where he was besieged again.

Diomedes Soter.subject: Ancient India

Ellora Caves.subject: Ancient India
Ellora Caves.question: The complex is a leading example of _____ rock-cut architecture, and several are not strictly "caves" in that they have no roof
Ellora Caves.fact: The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Aurangabad, India.  It is one of the largest rock-cut cave complexes in the world, with artwork dating from AD 600–1000, including Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain caves.  The complex is a leading example of Indian rock-cut architecture, and several are not strictly "caves" in that they have no roof.  Cave 16 features the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world, the Kailash temple, a chariot-shaped monument dedicated to the god Shiva.  The Kailash temple excavation also features sculptures depicting various Hindu deities as well as relief panels summarizing the two major Hindu epics.  There are over 100 caves at the site, all excavated from the basalt cliffs in the Charanandri Hills, 34 of which are open to public

Ellora Caves.subject: Ancient India
Ellora Caves.question: All of the _____ monuments were built during the Rashtrakuta dynasty (r
Ellora Caves.fact: There are over 100 caves at the site, all excavated from the basalt cliffs in the Charanandri Hills, 34 of which are open to public.  These consist of 17 Hindu (caves 13–29), 12 Buddhist (caves 1–12) and 5 Jain (caves 30–34) caves, each group representing deities and mythologies prevalent in the 1st millennium CE, as well as monasteries of each respective religion.  They were built close to one another and illustrate the religious harmony that existed in ancient India.  All of the Ellora monuments were built during the Rashtrakuta dynasty (r.  753-982 AD), which constructed part of the Hindu and Buddhist caves, and the Yadava dynasty (c.  1187–1317), which constructed a number of the Jain caves.  Funding for the construction of the monuments was provided by royals, traders and the wealthy of the region

Ellora Caves.fact: == Etymology == Ellora, also called Verul or Elura, is the short form of the ancient name Elloorpuram.  The older form of the name has been found in ancient references, such as the Baroda inscription of 812 AD, which mentions "the greatness of this edifice" and that "this great edifice was built on a hill by Krishnaraja at Elapura, the edifice in the inscription being the Kailasa temple.  In the Indian tradition, each cave is named and has a suffix Guha (Sanskrit), Lena, or Leni (Marathi), meaning cave.  It is also thought to be derived from Ilvalapuram, named after the asura Ilvala who ruled this region who was vanquished by Sage Agastya.  == Location == The Ellora caves are situated in state of Maharashtra about 29 km (18 mi) northwest of the city of Aurangabad, 300 km (190 mi) east-northeast of Mumbai, 235 km (146 mi) from Pune and about 100 km (62 mi) west of the Ajanta Caves another UNESCO World Heritage Site and 2. 4 mi) from Grishneshwar Temple (India).  Ellora occupies a relatively flat rocky region of the Western Ghats, where ancient volcanic activity had created multilayered basalt formations, known as the Deccan Traps

Ellora Caves.question: The disputes generally concern: one, whether the _____ or Hindu caves were carved first and, two, the relative dating of caves within a particular tradition
Ellora Caves.fact: The resulting vertical face made access to many layers of rock formations easier, enabling architects to pick basalt with finer grains for more detailed sculpting.  == Chronology == The construction at Ellora has been studied since British colonial rule.  However, the overlapping styles between the Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves has made it difficult to establish agreement concerning the chronology of their construction.  The disputes generally concern: one, whether the Buddhist or Hindu caves were carved first and, two, the relative dating of caves within a particular tradition.  The broad consensus that has emerged is based on comparing the carving styles at Ellora to other cave temples in the Deccan region that have been dated, textual records of various dynasties, and epigraphical evidence found at various archaeological sites near Ellora and elsewhere in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka.  Geri Hockfield Malandra and other scholars have stated that the Ellora caves had three important building periods: a Buddhist phase (~600 to 730 CE) and a later Hindu and Jain phase (~730 to 950 CE).  The earliest caves may have been built during the Traikutakas and Vakataka dynasti

Ellora Caves.subject: Ancient India
Ellora Caves.question: The monastery caves have shrines including carvings of _____, bodhisattvas and saints
Ellora Caves.fact: It was initially thought that the Buddhist caves were the earliest structures that were created between the fifth and eighth centuries, with caves 1–5 in the first phase (400–600) and 6–12 in the later phase (650–750), but modern scholars now consider the construction of Hindu caves to have been before the Buddhist caves.  The earliest Buddhist cave is Cave 6, then 5, 2, 3, 5 (right wing), 4, 7, 8, 10 and 9, with caves 11 and 12, also known as Do Thal and Tin Thal respectively, being the last.  Eleven out of the twelve Buddhist caves consist of viharas, or monasteries with prayer halls: large, multi-storeyed buildings carved into the mountain face, including living quarters, sleeping quarters, kitchens, and other rooms.  The monastery caves have shrines including carvings of Gautama Buddha, bodhisattvas and saints.  In some of these caves, sculptors have endeavoured to give the stone the look of wood.  Caves 5, 10, 11 and 12 are architecturally important Buddhist caves.  Cave 5 is unique among the Ellora caves as it was designed as a hall with a pair of parallel refectory benches in the centre and a Buddha statue in the rear

Ellora Caves.subject: Ancient India
Ellora Caves.question: In the apsidal end of the chaitya hall is a stupa on the face of which a colossal high seated _____ in vyakhyana mudra (teaching posture)
Ellora Caves.fact: It is the only dedicated chaitya griha amongst the Buddhist caves and is constructed along similar lines to Caves 19 and 26 of Ajanta.  Cave 10 also features a gavaksha, or chandrashala, arched window and a side connection to Cave 9 of Ellora.  The main hall of the Visvakarma cave is apsidal in plan and is divided into a central nave and side aisles by 28 octagonal columns with plain bracket capitals.  In the apsidal end of the chaitya hall is a stupa on the face of which a colossal high seated Buddha in vyakhyana mudra (teaching posture).  A large Bodhi tree is carved at his back.  The hall has a vaulted roof in which ribs (known as triforium) have been carved in the rock imitating the wooden ones.  The friezes above the pillars are Naga queens, and the extensive relief artwork shows characters such as entertainers, dancers and musicians

The corridor columns have massive squared shafts and ghata-pallava (vase and foliage) capitals.  The various levels of Cave 10 also feature idols of male and female deities, such as Maitreya, Tara, Avalokitesvara (Vajradhamma), Manjusri, Bhrkuti, and Mahamayuri, carved in the Pala dynasty style found in eastern regions of India.  Some southern Indian influences can also be found in various works in this cave.  == The Hindu monuments: Caves 13–29 == The Hindu caves were constructed during the Kalachuri period, from the mid-6th century to the end of the 8th century in two phases.  Nine cave temples were excavated early in the 6th century, followed by a further four caves (caves 17–29).  Work first started , in order, on Caves 28, 27 and 19 then Caves 29 and 21, which were excavated concurrently with Caves 20 and 26

The cave was completed prior to the ascension of Rashtrakuta dynasty which went on to expand the caves at Ellora. Farrukh Hormizd.fact: Rostam Farrokhzad, who was at that time stationed in Khorasan, succeeded him as the leader of the Pahlav. Azarmidokht was shortly afterwards blinded and killed by Rostam, who restored Boran to the throne.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: Farrukhsiyar (Persian: فرخ‌سیار, Persian pronunciation: [faɾ.ˈɾux saj.ˈjɑːɾ]; 20 August 1683 – 9 April 1719), also spelled as Farrukh Siyar, was the tenth Mughal Emperor from 1713 to 1719.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Farrukhsiyar (Persian: فرخ‌سیار, Persian pronunciation: [faɾ.ˈɾux saj.ˈjɑːɾ]; 20 August _____ – 9 April 1719), also spelled as Farrukh Siyar, was the tenth Mughal Emperor from 1713 to 1719
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Farrukhsiyar (Persian: فرخ‌سیار, Persian pronunciation: [faɾ.ˈɾux saj.ˈjɑːɾ]; 20 August 1683 – 9 April 1719), also spelled as Farrukh Siyar, was the tenth Mughal Emperor from 1713 to 1719.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: He rose to the throne after deposing his uncle _____
Farrukhsiyar.fact: He rose to the throne after deposing his uncle Jahandar Shah.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: He was an emperor only in name, with all effective power in the hands of the two courtiers, the _____ brothers
Farrukhsiyar.fact: He was an emperor only in name, with all effective power in the hands of the two courtiers, the Sayyid brothers.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: He was the second son of Azim-ush-Shan, the grandson of emperor _____ I and a great-grandson of emperor Aurangzeb
Farrukhsiyar.fact: He was the second son of Azim-ush-Shan, the grandson of emperor Bahadur Shah I and a great-grandson of emperor Aurangzeb.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: In _____, Farrukhsiyar accompanied his father on his campaign to Bengal
Farrukhsiyar.fact: In 1696, Farrukhsiyar accompanied his father on his campaign to Bengal.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Aurangzeb recalled Azim-ush-Shan from Bengal in _____ and instructed Farrukhsiyar to take charge of the province
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Aurangzeb recalled Azim-ush-Shan from Bengal in 1707 and instructed Farrukhsiyar to take charge of the province.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: In _____ Azim-ush-Shan anticipated Bahadur Shah I's death and a struggle for power, and recalled Farrukhsiyar
Farrukhsiyar.fact: In 1712 Azim-ush-Shan anticipated Bahadur Shah I's death and a struggle for power, and recalled Farrukhsiyar.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: He was marching past _____ (present-day Patna, Bihar, India) when he learned of the Mughal emperor's death
Farrukhsiyar.fact: He was marching past Azimabad (present-day Patna, Bihar, India) when he learned of the Mughal emperor's death.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: On 6 April, he learned of his father's defeat to an alliance orchestrated by _____ between Jahandar Shah, and his younger brothers Rafi-us-Shan and Jahan Shah
Farrukhsiyar.fact: On 6 April, he learned of his father's defeat to an alliance orchestrated by Zulfiqar Khan Nusrat Jung between Jahandar Shah, and his younger brothers Rafi-us-Shan and Jahan Shah.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Although the prince considered suicide, he was dissuaded by his friends from _____
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Although the prince considered suicide, he was dissuaded by his friends from Bengal. Farrukhsiyar wanted revenge for his father's death and was joined by Hussain Ali Khan (the subahdar of Bengal) and Abdullah Khan, his brother and the subahdar of Allahabad.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: When they reached Allahabad from Azimabad, Jahandar Shah's military general _____ and 12,000 troops clashed with Abdullah Khan, resulting in Abdullah retreating to the Allahabad Fort
Farrukhsiyar.fact: When they reached Allahabad from Azimabad, Jahandar Shah's military general Syed Abdul Ghaffar Khan Gardezi and 12,000 troops clashed with Abdullah Khan, resulting in Abdullah retreating to the Allahabad Fort.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: However, _____'s army fled when they learned about his death
Farrukhsiyar.fact: When they reached Allahabad from Azimabad, Jahandar Shah's military general Syed Abdul Ghaffar Khan Gardezi and 12,000 troops clashed with Abdullah Khan, resulting in Abdullah retreating to the Allahabad Fort. However, Gardezi's army fled when they learned about his death.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: After the defeat, _____ sent general Khwaja Ahsan Khan and his son Aazuddin
Farrukhsiyar.fact: When they reached Allahabad from Azimabad, Jahandar Shah's military general Syed Abdul Ghaffar Khan Gardezi and 12,000 troops clashed with Abdullah Khan, resulting in Abdullah retreating to the Allahabad Fort. After the defeat, Jahandar Shah sent general Khwaja Ahsan Khan and his son Aazuddin.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: On 10 January _____, Farrukhsiyar and Jahandar Shah's forces met at Samugarh, 14 kilometres (9 mi) east of Agra in present-day Uttar Pradesh
Farrukhsiyar.fact: On 10 January 1713, Farrukhsiyar and Jahandar Shah's forces met at Samugarh, 14 kilometres (9 mi) east of Agra in present-day Uttar Pradesh.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: His brother _____ became the Mir Bakhshi or Commander-in-Chief
Farrukhsiyar.fact: His brother Hussain Ali Khan became the Mir Bakhshi or Commander-in-Chief. Learning about these developments, the other Sayyid brother (Hussain Ali Khan) wrote to Abdullah Khan: "It was clear, from the Prince's talk and the nature of his acts, that he was a man who paid no regard to claims for service performed, one void of faith, a breaker of his word and altogether without shame".

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: However, the anti-_____ brothers faction in the Mughal emperor's court compelled him to send secret letters to Ajit Singh assuring him of rewards if he defeated Hussain Ali Khan
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Farrukhsiyar could not confront them, as the Sayyid Brothers maintained control of the strongest part of the army, and thus the latter became de facto rulers of the empire. However, the anti-Sayyid brothers faction in the Mughal emperor's court compelled him to send secret letters to Ajit Singh assuring him of rewards if he defeated Hussain Ali Khan.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: Hussain Ali Khan left Delhi for Ajmer on 6 January 1714, accompanied by Sarbuland Khan and Afrasyab Khan.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: As Hussain Ali Khan advanced to Ajmer via Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Merta, Ajit Singh retreated to the deserts hoping to dissuade the Mughal general from a battle.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: As Hussain Ali Khan advanced to Ajmer via Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Merta, Ajit Singh retreated to the deserts hoping to dissuade the Mughal general from a battle. As a result, Mughal authority was restored in Rajputana.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: His son, _____, was compelled to accompany him to see the Mughal emperor his brother-in-law
Farrukhsiyar.fact: His son, Kunwar Abhai Singh, was compelled to accompany him to see the Mughal emperor his brother-in-law.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: Taking advantage of the situation, the Jats advanced.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: In early 1713, Farrukhsiyar unsuccessfully sent subahdar of Agra, Chabela Ram to defeat the Jat leader Churaman.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: In December, Churaman's son, _____, marched from the fort and battled Jai Singh II; the Raja claimed victory
Farrukhsiyar.fact: In December, Churaman's son, Muhkam Singh, marched from the fort and battled Jai Singh II; the Raja claimed victory.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: With the Mughals running out of ammunition, Syed Muzaffar Khan was ordered to bring gunpowder, rockets and mounds of lead from the arsenal at Agra.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: By January _____, the siege had lasted for more than a year
Farrukhsiyar.fact: By January 1718, the siege had lasted for more than a year.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: With rain coming late in _____, prices of commodities increased and Raja Jai Singh II found it difficult to continue the siege
Farrukhsiyar.fact: With rain coming late in 1717, prices of commodities increased and Raja Jai Singh II found it difficult to continue the siege.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: On 19 April _____, Churaman was presented to Farrukhsiyar; they negotiated for peace, with Churaman accepting Mughal authority
Farrukhsiyar.fact: On 19 April 1718, Churaman was presented to Farrukhsiyar; they negotiated for peace, with Churaman accepting Mughal authority.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: Khan Jahan was given the title of Bahadur ("brave"). Mughal emperors Bahadur Shah I and Jahandar Shah failed to suppress Banda's uprising.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Mughal emperors _____ I and Jahandar Shah failed to suppress Banda's uprising
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Mughal emperors Bahadur Shah I and Jahandar Shah failed to suppress Banda's uprising.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: In _____, the Sirhind faujdar (garrison commander) Zainuddin Ahmad Khan attacked the Sikhs near Ropar
Farrukhsiyar.fact: In 1714, the Sirhind faujdar (garrison commander) Zainuddin Ahmad Khan attacked the Sikhs near Ropar.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: In _____, Farrukhisyar sent 20,000 troops under Qamaruddin Khan, Abdus Samad Khan and Zakariya Khan Bahadur to defeat Bahadur
Farrukhsiyar.fact: In 1715, Farrukhisyar sent 20,000 troops under Qamaruddin Khan, Abdus Samad Khan and Zakariya Khan Bahadur to defeat Bahadur.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: After an eight-month siege at Gurdaspur, _____ surrendered after he ran out of ammunition
Farrukhsiyar.fact: After an eight-month siege at Gurdaspur, Banda Singh Bahadur surrendered after he ran out of ammunition. Banda Singh Bahadur and his 200 companions were arrested and brought to Delhi; he was paraded around the city of Sirhind.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Banda Singh Bahadur and his 200 companions were arrested and brought to Delhi; he was paraded around the city of _____
Farrukhsiyar.fact: In 1714, the Sirhind faujdar (garrison commander) Zainuddin Ahmad Khan attacked the Sikhs near Ropar. Banda Singh Bahadur and his 200 companions were arrested and brought to Delhi; he was paraded around the city of Sirhind.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Banda Singh Bahadur was put into an iron cage and the remaining _____ were chained
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Banda Singh Bahadur was put into an iron cage and the remaining Sikhs were chained. Although the emperor promised to spare the Sikhs who converted to Islam, according to William Irvine "not one prisoner proved false to his faith".

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: They were pressured to give up their faith and become _____
Farrukhsiyar.fact: They were pressured to give up their faith and become Muslims.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Although the emperor promised to spare the Sikhs who converted to Islam, according to _____ "not one prisoner proved false to his faith"
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Although the emperor promised to spare the Sikhs who converted to Islam, according to William Irvine "not one prisoner proved false to his faith".

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: The _____s were brought to Delhi in a procession with the 780 Sikh prisoners, 2,000 Sikh heads hung on spears, and 700 cartloads of heads of slaughtered Sikhs used to terrorise the population
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Although the emperor promised to spare the Sikhs who converted to Islam, according to William Irvine "not one prisoner proved false to his faith". The Sikhs were brought to Delhi in a procession with the 780 Sikh prisoners, 2,000 Sikh heads hung on spears, and 700 cartloads of heads of slaughtered Sikhs used to terrorise the population.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: After three months of confinement, on 19 June _____ Farrukhsiyar had Banda Singh Bahadur and his followers executed, despite the wealthy Khatris of Delhi offering money for his release
Farrukhsiyar.fact: After three months of confinement, on 19 June 1716 Farrukhsiyar had Banda Singh Bahadur and his followers executed, despite the wealthy Khatris of Delhi offering money for his release.

Farrukhsiyar.fact: He was executed on the order of Farrukhsiyar in 1718.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: This was because he needed a close party of supporters who were directly related to him in dealing with the _____ brothers
Farrukhsiyar.fact: This was because he needed a close party of supporters who were directly related to him in dealing with the Sayyid brothers.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Inayatullah Khan was appointed the Diwan-i-Tan-o Khalisa, and the governor of Kashmir in _____
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Inayatullah Khan was appointed the Diwan-i-Tan-o Khalisa, and the governor of Kashmir in 1717.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: He set fire to the Hindu area of _____ and forbade the Pandits from wearing turbans
Farrukhsiyar.fact: He set fire to the Hindu area of Srinagar and forbade the Pandits from wearing turbans.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Inayatullah Khan was further responsible for the re-imposition of Jizyah in the _____ after the death of Aurangzeb
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Inayatullah Khan was further responsible for the re-imposition of Jizyah in the Mughal Empire after the death of Aurangzeb.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: The farman allowed the _____ company to carry out duty-free trade in the province of Bengal
Farrukhsiyar.fact: The farman allowed the British East India company to carry out duty-free trade in the province of Bengal. The improper use of dastaks for company officials' own private trade angered the Nawab of Bengal, Alivardi Khan, which eventually led to future conflicts of the Nawabs of Bengal with the British East India company.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Mir Jumla III began approving proposals for jagirs and mansabs without consulting _____, the prime minister
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Mir Jumla III began approving proposals for jagirs and mansabs without consulting Syed Abdullah, the prime minister. Syed Abdullah's deputy Ratan Chand accepted bribes for him to do work and was involved in revenue farming, which was forbidden by the Mughal emperor.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Arriving at the Deccan, Syed Hussain made a treaty with Maratha ruler Shahu I in February _____
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Arriving at the Deccan, Syed Hussain made a treaty with Maratha ruler Shahu I in February 1718.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: Shahu was allowed to collect sardeshmukhi in Deccan, and received the lands of Berar and Gondwana to govern.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: In return, Shahu agreed to pay one million rupees annually and maintain an army of 15,000 horses for the Sayyids.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: The title of bakshi was first conferred on Hussain Ali Khan (with the titles of Umdat-ul-Mulk, Amir-ul-umara and Bahadur Firuz Jung) and then to Chin Qilich Khan and Afrasayab Khan Bahadur.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: Taqi, from the _____ province of Mazandaran, married the daughter of Masum Khan Safawi; if she was the mother of Fakhr-un-nissa, this would account for her daughter's selection as the prince's wife
Farrukhsiyar.fact: Taqi, from the Persian province of Mazandaran, married the daughter of Masum Khan Safawi; if she was the mother of Fakhr-un-nissa, this would account for her daughter's selection as the prince's wife.

Farrukhsiyar.question: His second wife was _____, the daughter of Maharajah Ajit Singh
Farrukhsiyar.fact: His second wife was Bai Indira Kanwar, the daughter of Maharajah Ajit Singh.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: She married Farrukhsiyar on 27 September _____, during the fourth year of his reign, and they had no children

Farrukhsiyar.fact: After Farrukhsiyar's deposition and death she left the imperial harem on 16 July 1719, she returned to her father with her property and lived her remaining years in Jodhpur.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: In _____, in response to a message from the Mufti of Delhi, her brother Kirat Singh sent her to Delhi with her brother Mian Muhammad Khan
Farrukhsiyar.fact: In 1717, in response to a message from the Mufti of Delhi, her brother Kirat Singh sent her to Delhi with her brother Mian Muhammad Khan. Farrukhsiyar married her, and she entered the imperial harem on 3 July 1717.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: In 1717, in response to a message from the Mufti of Delhi, her brother Kirat Singh sent her to Delhi with her brother Mian Muhammad Khan. Farrukhsiyar married her, and she entered the imperial harem on 3 July 1717.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India

Farrukhsiyar.fact: Posthumously, he was called "Shahid-i-marhum" (the martyr received with mercy).

Farrukhsiyar.fact: There are 116 coins from his reign on display at the Lahore Museum and the Indian Museum in Kolkata.

Farrukhsiyar.fact: The coins were minted in Kabul, Kashmir, Ajmer, Allahabad, Bidar and Berar.

Farrukhsiyar.fact: The emperor and his top minister had been at odds for a long time, but tensions grew when the emperor broke an earlier agreement by appointing new officials in the Deccan region.

Farrukhsiyar.fact: Soon, the emperor found himself with only a small force of Rajput soldiers by the side of Jai Singh Kachhwaha.

Farrukhsiyar.fact: Abdullah Khan then called on his brother, Husain Ali Khan, to bring reinforcements from the Deccan. In October, Husain Ali Khan marched north with a large force of cavalry, infantry armed with matchlocks, and artillery.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: In October, _____ marched north with a large force of cavalry, infantry armed with matchlocks, and artillery

Farrukhsiyar.fact: He was joined by Balaji Vishwanath, a Maratha chief minister, who added Maratha horsemen to the army.

Farrukhsiyar.subject: Ancient India
Farrukhsiyar.question: In February _____, Husain Ali Khan made a dramatic entrance into Delhi, ignoring the formal court rules
Farrukhsiyar.fact: In February 1719, Husain Ali Khan made a dramatic entrance into Delhi, ignoring the formal court rules.

Farrukhsiyar.fact: Seeing that they could not simply install one of their own, the powerful Sayyid brothers chose to replace the emperor with a young and manageable prince.

Farrukhsiyar.fact: Upon his death, Ajit Singh reclaimed his widowed daughter along with dowry and returned to Jodhpur.
